mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: cmd.c parse() committed a count leaving gm.multi above 0 before a nonmovement row this port will not repeat, which allmain.c moveloop_core():515-531 turns into a repeat of the command; that nonmovement command path remains unsupported

summary: The remaining screen is blocked by js/cmd.js rhack() rejecting a count-prefixed nonmovement command before it dispatches the already implemented pickup path. C parse() sets command_count=5 and gm.multi=4, but the comma binding reaches hack.c:dopickup(), which copies command_count and immediately sets gm.multi=0 before calling pickup(-count). This is one counted pickup, not an automatic repeat. The actionable scope is a divergence fix to the cmd.c:rhack() count gate; the saved queue annotation naming parse()/moveloop_core() as the refusal owner is too broad.

source.branch: For a count-prefixed comma command on a reachable floor square with one five-dagger stack, cmd.c:parse() leaves gc.command_count=5 and gm.multi=4. The comma row at cmd.c:1799 binds to dopickup; cmd.c:rhack() calls the bound function without a count-specific refusal. hack.c:dopickup() copies gc.command_count, sets gm.multi=0, and calls pickup(-count), so this handler consumes the count as the requested item quantity and prevents moveloop_core() from repeating it. In js/cmd.js, the generic state.multi > 0 nonmovement guard rejects the command before runPickupCommand() reaches js/hack.js:dopickup() and js/pickup.js:pickup(). The mismatch is an overbroad refusal in an implemented command path, not a missing pickup selection function.
callers: allmain.c:moveloop_core() calls rhack(0) for a fresh command and rhack(gc.cmd_key) for a pending positive count (515-531); js/allmain.js:moveloop_core() maps these to rhack(0) and rhack(g.cmdKey) (1701-1706).

cmd.c:rhack() calls parse() on a fresh command, then resolves the comma binding and invokes its function pointer (3652-3654, 3679-3685, 3724-3748); js/cmd.js:rhack() calls parseCommand(), maps the comma key to pickup, and currently refuses at the counted-command guard before dispatch (5373-5381, 5503-5527, 5858-5878).

cmd.c:1799 binds comma to dopickup; hack.c:dopickup() calls pickup_checks() and pickup(-count) (3876-3891); js/cmd.js:runPickupCommand() dispatches js/hack.js:dopickup(), which calls pickup_checks() and js/pickup.js:pickup() (js/cmd.js:3435-3441, 5873-5878; js/hack.js:4344-4362).
dependencies: cmd.c:parse() (5096-5149) reads the command count, stores it in gc.command_count, assigns gm.multi, and decrements gm.multi once. js/cmd.js:parse() already maps these values to state.commandCount and state.multi.

hack.c:dopickup() (3876-3891) consumes gc.command_count and clears gm.multi before calling pickup(-count); js/hack.js:dopickup() already preserves both transitions, although its comment says counts above one cannot arrive because of the guard.

pickup.c:pickup() (693-696, 759-772, 809-817, 894-910) consumes a negative quantity and returns whether an item was tried. js/pickup.js:pickup() already has the counted menu path and the single-floor-stack path; pickup_object() and capacity preflight remain runtime dependencies for the selected stack.

hack.c:pickup_checks() (3788-3871) has the ordinary reachable floor-pile result required here. Its swallowed/loot_mon, pool, lava, and cannot-reach-floor paths remain unsupported in js/hack.js, but the recipe uses a reachable floor pile with an object and does not enter those arms.

pickup.c:pickup() conditionally calls mon.c:hideunder() in its floor tail (894-897). js/pickup.js retains note_unported('mon.c hideunder') only when hides_under() is true; the recipe uses a human Valkyrie, so this gap is not active for this case.

evidence: The saved baseline challenges/evaluations/20261001125731-v16.json records the same input recipe SHA-256 0a09274f8f3f58135a4d6d5d759a56ddf49ebc7d94d3d726f04836d36e6cd3bf and recording SHA-256 ee7bcb39d33542a91a57da34fd5f4bfe33f549ace7c066e8b9ca5aa0b2353ecb. Its first mismatch is a stop at segment 0, step 26 (comma): 26/27 screens and cursors match; C has 2267 RNG calls versus JS 2251. The message is the generic counted nonmovement refusal from js/cmd.js; no pickup function has run yet.

The admitted v16 manifest case wizard-picks-up-five-dropped-daggers identifies the reached C behavior as pickup.c:pickup: one count-prefixed command collects the floor stack and spends a turn. The input-only recipe is challenges/cases/v16/wizard-picks-up-five-dropped-daggers.recipe.session.json; the immutable C recording is challenges/cases/v16/wizard-picks-up-five-dropped-daggers.session.json. The saved evaluation records an independent C replay as byte-identical to that recording.

Upstream cmd.c:parse() at 5096-5149 sets gc.command_count from the 5 prefix and then sets gm.multi to 4. Upstream cmd.c:rhack() at 3627-3843 resolves the comma binding and calls its function at 3724-3748 without rejecting a positive gm.multi. The command table at 1799 binds comma to dopickup.

Upstream hack.c:dopickup() at 3876-3891 copies gc.command_count to count, immediately clears gm.multi, then calls pickup(-count) after pickup_checks() succeeds. Thus this input never reaches allmain.c:moveloop_core() repeat handling for positive multi. Upstream pickup.c:pickup() at 693-696 interprets the negative argument as an item count and at 809-817 picks min(stack quantity, count) for a single traditional floor object; the menu path sets the requested count at 763-772.

At examined commit fa7aad456f8e2071d96ec4f804c9ecdae6a898d2, js/cmd.js:rhack() has the generic refusal at 5503-5527 before the pickup dispatch at 5858-5878. js/hack.js:dopickup() at 4347-4362 already copies state.commandCount, clears state.multi, and calls js/pickup.js:pickup(-count). The code comment at js/hack.js:4351-4352 documents why the guard currently blocks larger counts.

The source patch series is limited to deterministic runtime, stable sorting, RNG logging, and terminal capture according to nethack-c/patches/README.md; searching nethack-c/patches for cmd.c, hack.c, pickup.c, and allmain.c finds no edits to these gameplay functions. The actionable difference therefore lies in JavaScript command admission, not recorder patch behavior.
